The /for/ceo page, top to bottom. NEW = needs layout from website. Copy: alex-voice run 2026-11-04-01-ceo-page-4nov, attempt 2, graded Good (open: OPEN-32, the opening); the run halted on a grader citation error, so attempt 3 didn't run.
1. title (NEW): the page's headline, 57 characters. Use it as the <title> and link-preview title in place of "Hi Stepan: a page for you, from Alex Alderman". Show it in the hero above "Hi Štěpán," (eyebrow or H1, website's call). Set lang="cs" on its Czech half. Optional data change: name "Štěpán Hykš", so the hello is "Hi Štěpán," (the hello is the first word of name) and the portrait caption matches.
2. Hero lead (P1, extended): landing.lead, then landing.lead_quote.cz as a short quote with landing.lead_quote.en directly under it as its gloss (NEW: a small quote element inside the lead; Czech in lang="cs"; gloss in plain or muted type), then landing.lead_after. landing.greeting is put together from these four for the link-preview description.
3. Read it in Claude (NEW, prominent, right after the lead): landing.agent.line, then a button (landing.agent.button) that opens claude.ai/new?q= with agent.ceo.prompt, then a smaller Copy-the-prompt control for other AIs, labelled landing.agent.alt.
4. The person (NEW band): landing.person.heading and landing.person.body. Paragraphs are split on blank lines, and it has a six-item bulleted list, which Rich() in personal.tsx can't render yet.
5. The join (NEW, a short band or pull line): landing.join.heading and landing.join.body. It replaces the old P2 note band.
6. The argument: landing.argument.heading and landing.argument.body.
7. The strategy: landing.strategy.heading and landing.strategy.body.
8. How it runs: landing.how.heading and landing.how.body.
9. The quarters (NEW: a four-step row or timeline): landing.plan.heading, landing.plan.intro, the steps landing.plan.q1 to q4, then landing.plan.close.
10. The offer: landing.offer.heading and landing.offer.body. No numbers.
11. Proof: landing.proof.heading, then landing.proof.switch, landing.proof.workflows (link "The 36 GetSales workflows" to /articles/36-outbound-workflows-and-the-one-variable-behind-them) and landing.proof.agent ("/llms.txt" links to /llms.txt), then landing.proof.agent_command as a copyable code line.
12. Concerns: the existing {q, lead, a} shape, four items. The live template (personal.tsx) doesn't render concerns, so website adds the Concerns block from page.tsx with its fixed heading "What I'm guessing you're concerned with".
13. The CRM band ("Imagine your conversion rate...", existing): keep.
14. P5 made line (existing text, unchanged).
15. P6 carousel: replace recommend.json's ceo list with recommend.ceo[0..3] (id, why, fallback). All four ids have live pages, and the pipeline article (art-pipeline-promise) is gone from it (W199).
16. landing.reading_list: personal.tsx doesn't render it. RULES.md rule 5 bans minute counters, and alex-voice bans the heading "Your reading list". Render it without minutes and without that heading, or leave it unrendered: the carousel and the agent route already cover these links.
17. Agent row and P7 notice (existing). sources has new text.
Remove from this page (labour framing, W199): the CEO lens band in lens.tsx (CeoLens: "Where the return comes from" / "Keeping everyone takes the biggest saving off the table", the S10-c "keep their promise" clip and its three labour-cost quotes). Also remove the old P2 note text and the evidence band of four step cards: proof (11) covers it. The P4 quote collection ("What it costs to keep running, and how I kept the keys safe") is optional; drop it to keep the page short. for.lens.ceo (site-copy.json) replaces "Where the return on AI comes from if nobody gets cut" on the /for grid and in the agent track.
Agent track (NEW): /for/ceo/llms.txt returns 404 today. It should be agent.ceo.guide_intro, then agent.ceo.order as a numbered list of links, each with its why line. agent.ceo.prompt has that URL filled in.
Flags for website and orchestration: /log.md opens on "we're not going to fire half the team". Every page's "Where next" list links the pipeline article ("If AI isn't lowering your labor costs..."), and the /llms.txt summary says "cut labor or increase revenue". So the CEO's AI still meets the labour line one click away. Old fields: framing and note are required by app/stakeholders.ts and now hold graded copy. ask.short, ask.heading and ask.body are required there too and still hold an ask and the word "demo". The live template doesn't render them, but website should drop that check or empty them (rule 11).
title: Po nocích s CC nestíháte? Make it someone's full-time job
name: Štěpán Hykš
landing.greeting: Hi Štěpán. In September you wrote: „jednoduše to všechno už sami po nocích s CC nestíháme :)“ (We just can't keep up with it all ourselves any more, even working nights with Claude Code.) And Addvery wants to grow five times. I think both problems have the same answer, and it starts with revenue.
landing.lead_quote.cz: „jednoduše to všechno už sami po nocích s CC nestíháme :)“
landing.lead_quote.en: We just can't keep up with it all ourselves any more, even working nights with Claude Code.
landing.lead_after: And Addvery wants to grow five times. I think both problems have the same answer, and it starts with revenue.
landing.agent.line: You already work with Claude, so you can read this page there too: the main point in three lines, in Czech or English. Then you choose what to open.
landing.agent.alt: Use another AI? Copy the prompt.
landing.person.heading: For nine months, it's been my full-time job
landing.person.body:
I took an AI sabbatical. For nine months I've done nothing but build in Claude Code, 40 to 50 hours a week.

This site is what that looks like. Most of it was built in one recorded day:

- About a dozen Claude Code sessions ran in the background at once, each with one role, its own folder and its own rules.
- All of them worked from one written plan.
- Every question for me went to one desk, one at a time.
- Before a session ran out of context, it handed over to a fresh one.
- 18 reusable skills came out of it. The one that writes in my voice has its own grader.
- The site has a second version for AI agents, with a public MCP server.

Not everything went well. I deleted one session I didn't need, and the command ended all seven in that folder. Now there's a skill that brings them back. (A fun way to learn, honestly.)
landing.join.heading: Your backlog and your revenue goal have one answer
landing.join.body: **Someone who runs Claude Code at full capacity, as their whole job,** pointed at pipeline first. That's where five times comes from.
landing.argument.heading: Inbound alone is too slow for five times
landing.argument.body:
Ivana wrote in October that Addvery is at roughly 200 million CZK, and the next goal is 1 billion. Five times.

Inbound marketing is great, but its first signed deals take a long time. Five times needs them sooner.

There's no sales team yet: Ivana is building it from scratch, and good business developers are very hard to hire in this sector right now. **So what you have is consultants.** They're the resource to generate revenue from, and they're already here. So I'd start now.
landing.strategy.heading: Hear about the RFP before it's published
landing.strategy.body:
You don't need more decision makers in your inbox. **You need people close enough to the work to know when an RFP is coming,** and to tell you early: CRM and loyalty leads, project managers, people around procurement. Not the C-suite.

First the relationship. Then you hear about the RFP before it's published, help shape it, and win it.

You already have this network. Your consultants work inside client companies, so they hear about the next project first. People who used to work at Addvery now work at clients and buyers. It just isn't part of sales yet.
landing.how.heading: It runs from your consultants' own accounts
landing.how.body:
The messages go out from your consultants' own LinkedIn accounts, and I run the system. Agents research each account and write the drafts. **Every consultant approves what goes out from their account.** About 20 senior accounts are enough.

The language follows the market: Czech or Slovak at home, English abroad. I've run outreach in both Czech and English.

It fits what Ivana is building, too. Her agents already flag companies worth calling (her post of 31 October). This gives those flags people to call, and a number to measure: booked calls.

Then the city sprint: two or three days in one city, with no conference. Eight to ten meetings a day in person, booked over six weeks of outreach before the trip. Your leaders already travel, like Singapore for SWITCH. The sprint fills those days.
landing.plan.heading: What happens each quarter
landing.plan.intro: Honestly, nothing gets booked in the first six to eight weeks. LinkedIn's limits grow with each account's own activity, so every account starts slowly. Going from zero to full volume gets accounts blocked. And getting about 20 people to agree takes time. **So I won't promise you meetings in 30 days.**
landing.plan.q1: First quarter, setup: the consultants agree, their accounts warm up, and I build the target list and the system.
landing.plan.q2: Then booking: six weeks of outreach before each trip.
landing.plan.q3: Around month three or four: the first city sprint.
landing.plan.close: That's why I'd start now. Every month of waiting moves the first sprint a month later.
landing.offer.heading: How I'd charge for it
landing.offer.body: A setup fee for the first quarter. After that, **you pay per booked call, and only for booked calls.** What counts as a booked call sets the price.
landing.proof.heading: Things you can check yourself
landing.proof.switch: Your point at SWITCH was to first map how the company really works, then put agents with owners on it. This site ran that way: the plan was the map, every session had one job, and every question came to one human. Me.
landing.proof.workflows: The 36 GetSales workflows I built for Addvery: four customer types from your own case studies, in Czech, English and German, with three approaches each. Each one opens with a message written for its lead. Nothing sends.
landing.proof.agent: And the agent version: give any AI the map at /llms.txt, or connect the site to Claude Code:
landing.proof.agent_command: claude mcp add --transport http alex-alderman https://hire-me-hackathon.vercel.app/mcp
landing.concerns[0].a: Booking starts once the accounts are ready, and the first city sprint comes around month three or four. That's why the setup fee covers only the first quarter.
landing.concerns[1].q: My consultants are busy at clients. Will they do this?
landing.concerns[1].lead: Not all of them, and that's fine.
landing.concerns[1].a: About 20 senior accounts are enough, and each consultant only approves drafts. Getting them to agree is the slowest step, so it starts first.
landing.concerns[2].lead: It should sound like each consultant.
landing.concerns[2].a: Nothing goes out without the consultant's yes, so it has to sound like them. This site's copy works the same way: my voice skill writes it, and a separate grader checks it.
landing.concerns[3].a: Over a decade in the Czech Republic, long-term residency and a trade licence. My Czech is B1 to B2.
landing.made_line: This page came out of a reusable skill. Once it's built it's built: point it at your top 100 accounts and every decision-maker gets one.

agent.ceo.prompt: Read https://hire-me-hackathon.vercel.app/for/ceo/llms.txt and follow its guide. It's a hire-me page made for Addvery's CEO. Give me the main point in three lines first, then ask me what I want to look at.
agent.ceo.guide_intro: You're showing Addvery's CEO around a page I made for him. I'm a GTM engineer, applying to Addvery. He's busy, so give him the point in three lines first. One: his AI backlog and his revenue goal have one answer, someone who runs Claude Code at full capacity. Two: I'd point it at pipeline first, through his consultants' own LinkedIn accounts. Three: it runs by quarters, with the first city sprint around month three or four. Then ask what he wants to look at. If he writes in Czech, answer in Czech. Link every claim to its page (each page's "Human version" link). Never ask him to contact me.
